body:
<!-- pr-reviewer: 2407d9b09dc671834bfc6fd7d67d564bd8adc437 -->

**Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

The PR re-pins the `pocket3d_hsm` bore counts and the Linux mesh facet count after the solidcore bump of PR #3802, with proof. It changes no product code.

## What looks good

- The pin update is minimal and honest: `BORE_PIN` = (4688, 4660, 1980) replaces (3158, 3130, 1141) on the three measured platforms, and `BORE_PIN_BEFORE_3802` = (3158, 3130, 1141) is added so the exactness tests now reject the reading from before the bump.
- The Linux mesh facet pin 6228 -> 5232 is Linux-only, matches the author's probe table, and the comment on the pin names df899f029 and 940cc5d0e.
- The exactness tests reject the pre-bump reading and the old truck-mesh readings, and the heavy test keeps its `#[ignore = "heavy lane: ..."]` marker untouched.
- The decision doc (`docs/decisions/3886-pocket3d-hsm-pin.md`) records the decision, the why (first bad commit df899f029, the probe table, the per-level plan table), what was considered and dropped (fix of plan B -> #4010, widened band, plain ignore, revert), what is not measured, and the cost to change later.
- The PR body names the author's green quick gate, heavy step and light lane, and says what was not exercised (Windows/macOS runs of the updated test).
- The long-plan defect (plan B, 3x feed length, filed as #4010, P3, effort:max) is explicitly not fixed here - the right call for an 3d test pin.

## Results merged with main

Runner (self-hosted `camcraft-pr-test`): https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/actions/runs/45635851270 - main 9caa0d572.

- Trial merge with main: clean, 2 files differ from main.
- Quick gate: `app suites: pocket3d_hsm` ok (38s), 0 failed, 0 stalled.
- Clippy: `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.
- Light lane (local worktree on the trial-merged tree, release): 6 of 6 steps ok, 0 failed, 0 stalled (wall 9.8 min): light build, motion light: lib, adaptive_troch_island, adaptive_troch_neck, adaptive_troch_parallel, pocket_pass_start.
- The author's heavy step (`app heavy: pocket3d_hsm`, Linux x86_64, release) is named in the body as ok on this head. It is not required for a P2 PR, and the reviewer did not re-run it.

## Requested before merge

None.

## Notes / questions (not blocking)

- The 5232-facet mesh pin lives inside `user_job()`, which is used only by the ignored heavy test. So the runner's quick gate green does not exercise it; the 5232 pin rests on the author's release-tier run (named in the body). The exactness tests on the runner verify the pin logic only.
- The PR body says PR #3802 "changes Cargo.lock, crates/kernel/Cargo.toml and geometry/src/step_diag.rs" - it also changed the root Cargo.toml (truck-polymesh removed), assets/ui/LICENSES.md and several test files. No planner code changed, which is the claim that matters.
- The macOS arm64 pin is not measured after the bump; it follows Windows and Linux (noted in the body and the decision doc). A macOS run must confirm it.
- The fallback band for unmeasured platforms ((4706..=4736) moves, (4678..=4708) planar, (539..=559) arcs) is stale relative to BORE_PIN (4688, 4660, 1980) - it was already stale before this PR (it held the truck-mesh era reading). Not this PR's change; worth a follow-up.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
